topic: October 2026 US chip-stock selloff: is the AI bubble cracking?

claims.claim: The PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell for 8 straight sessions (Oct 7-16, 2026), its longest losing streak since October 2008. It fell 3.83% on Fri Oct 16 to close at 11,137.29, with all 30 constituents lower. Investing.com says it was down 16% since its last advance on Oct 6.

claims.claim: SOX fell 15.7% from its Oct 6 close of 13,217.82 to 11,137.29 on Oct 16 (sessions Oct 7, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16). It was 23.9% below its June 22 record close of 14,634.72. The last equal-length run was Oct 1-10, 2008 (8 sessions, -19.8%). Secondary source; the math checks out (1 - 11137.29/13217.82 = 15.74%).

sources.title: Chip stocks fall an eighth straight day, a streak not seen since 2008

claims.claim: As of this research (Oct 19, 2026), no source reports Monday Oct 19 US trading. The streak stood at 8 sessions through the Fri Oct 16 close. The Oct 15 Yahoo Finance live blog flagged it as 'on track for an eight straight down day', the longest since October 2008.

claims.claim: Stated causes: (1) doubts about AI spending payoff, including a report that OpenAI's annualized revenue was near $50B versus earlier estimates of $70B; (2) debt-financed AI data centres and neoclouds, with CoreWeave carrying about $50B of debt and bond yields above 15%; (3) hot September CPI of 3.7% YoY and about a 92% priced chance of another Fed hike, with the 10-yr yield at 5.10% on Oct 15 and WTI at $101.91; (4) China's CXMT memory breakthrough raising price-war fears; (5) Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's 'casino' remarks.

claims.claim: UBS CIO, Oct 14: the selloff is 'more of a recalibration of expectations than a fundamental break in the AI investment story.' UBS cited about 28% expected S&P 500 earnings growth and semiconductor valuations below long-term averages. The quote is attributed to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi in secondary reports.

claims.claim: Jensen Huang, Oct 16, Berlin, to Bloomberg (reported as an interview with Emily Chang): 'All of this is going to pass, and the reason for that is very simple.' He also said: 'It's going to be transformative... There's no question it will continue, and we're at the beginning of that.' Bloomberg's original is paywalled; read via syndication.

claims.claim: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan, DBS Asia Future Forward Conference, Singapore, Oct 12: 'A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in.' He said investors 'set very extreme expectations only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino.' He also said capital 'might be the biggest constraint' on AI.

claims.claim: AI capex: Goldman Sachs puts Big Tech capital spending at roughly $800B this year (via BeInCrypto). Nvidia management cited top-5 hyperscaler capex of $1.3T expected in 2027.
